text.p: VIENNA, July 17 (Reuter) The main stories in the Austrian press this Thursday are:
DER STANDARD
- Vienna will be central to the U.N.'s fight against crime, according to the plans of U.N. General Secretary Kofi Annan.
- Steelmaker VA-Tech is ready to go shopping with a fund of eight billion schillings for company acquisitions, says Financial Director Helmuth Hamminger.
- The Greens expect that controversial foreign minister and People's Party leader Wolfgang Schuessel will have to resign for the sake of his party.
- Mobilkom Austria and Italian Stet have registered 169,000 new mobile phones in the first half of 1997, more than double last year's total.

- Mayr-Melnhof, European market leader in production of cartons and collapsible boxes, could only slightly increase its turnover in the first half of 1997 from the first half figure last year of 5.3 billion schillings.
- British financial magazine Euromoney presented Bank Austria with its "Award of Excellence", which it awards once a year the bank it considers the best in a country.
- Economy Minister Johannes Farnleitner's proposals for reforming the energy market are disputed.
DIE PRESSE
- The Greens are demanding a reduction in the president's power, while the Social Democrats are debating whether they should put forward their own presidential candidate.
- Austria will have no option but to join EMU assuming France and Germany also take part, says Bernhard Felderer, head of the Institute for Higher Studies.
- The Austrian National Bank will have to report to parliament twice a year in future, according to a new law based on a U.S. model.

- Austria is competitive. Slower wage growth in industry and schilling weakness has had a positive effect. Austria is seeing increased productivity and through investment in rationalisation, says Alois Guger, expert at the WIFO Institute for Economic Research.
- Ten percent of Austrians now have a mobile phone.
- Former Austrian finance minister Ferdinand Lacina will become Chancellor Viktor Klima's special envoy to the European Union on employment issues.

- EVN Energie Versorgung Niederoesterreich reported an 11.9 percent drop in pre-tax profit in the first nine months to 1.92 billion schillings. The reason was a normal winter this year after a colder one in 1995/6.
- The state prosecution could become involved in a dispute between Armani and the discount opticians Diskonter over fake Armani glasses.
KURIER
- People taking early retirement are likely to have to reckon with supplementary premiums in future. The social ministry is considering a two percent reduction for every year.
- A fourteen year old Tyrolean girl was murdered in Turkey.
- Austrians feel the government has not done enough to inform them about EMU.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- Doctors have lost thousands of patients since the introduction of a medical insurance record card fee.
- Austria's shopping centres are increasing their share of the market, taking 12 percent of the single trade volume last year.
- Austria's automobile suppliers are combining important parts of their research and development activities to improve their position in the world market.
- The number of private bankruptcies has risen by a fifth.

- Tractor maker Steyr Landmaschinentechnik, taken over last year by U.S.-based agricultural and construction equipment maker Case Corp, says exports have risen significantly and gets and is now looking towards eastern European markets.
